candidates.rationale: DuPont divergence: when a firm's ROE rank exceeds its ROA rank, profitability is leverage-driven rather than efficiency-driven, a quality-of-earnings red flag predicting weaker forward returns.
Erratic year-over-year swings in leverage signal weak financial-policy discipline and covenant/refinancing risk, predicting lower returns than firms with a stable capital structure.
A stale one-year high in book value per share flags ongoing equity erosion from losses, write-downs or buybacks that the market is slow to price as balance-sheet risk.
Asset turnover sitting near its own two-year high isolates a genuine within-firm efficiency improvement from industry-wide effects, a regime shift that should precede margin gains.

Staggered peer earnings reports continuously reshuffle relative profitability rank; a stock's rank rising over the past month flags improving competitive standing before slower fundamental investors react.
High-margin firms whose relative trading liquidity is accelerating are being newly discovered, timing entry to the start of a re-rating rather than after it.
Leverage and return volatility compound: a spike in price risk at an already-levered firm triggers forced de-risking and selling pressure, a short-lived distress effect.
Cheap-and-profitable stocks (high book-to-price, high ROE) identify quality the market is mispricing as a value trap, the documented quality-value premium.
A multi-quarter efficiency improvement sustained in a name with persistently high relative liquidity is more likely to be recognized and rewarded than the same gain in a thinly-traded stock.
Year-over-year EPS growth not yet matched by trailing price performance is unresolved good news, a post-earnings-drift setup predicting future price convergence.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

  TS_DELTA($close, 7)   (in 4 published alphas)

  ((DELAY($close, 20) - DELAY($close, 10)) / 10)   (in 3 published alphas)

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Very short deltas (5-day) on slow-moving fundamentals (accrual_gap) scored among the weakest (|t| 0.55). Slow-moving fields need longer differencing windows to carry signal.
  2. Five of fifteen rejects duplicated 9 to 15 nodes of one already-archived stochastic-range / dollar-volume-range subtree. That lineage is saturated; branch into new structural forms instead of recombining it further.
  3. A bare field proposed next to its own rank transform ($roa vs RANK($roa)) is a near-guaranteed correlation reject (rho about 1.0). Changing only the wrapper around an already-archived field is not a new signal.
  4. One reject used plain RANK instead of CS_RANK on a 252-day roa mean. Verify cross-sectional operators are applied consistently so rejections reflect true signal quality, not an operator slip.
  5. CS_RANK($close - TS_MAX($high, 21)) and CS_RANK($close / (TS_MAX($high, 21) + 1e-8)) mix adjusted $close with raw $high, yet both were accepted this round with the 2nd and 3rd highest fitness (4.553, 4.780). Given the known adjusted-vs-raw scale mismatch, audit whether that mixing inflated their scores before trusting them further, and flag any new $close-vs-$open/$high/$low expression the same way.
  6. TS_DELTA of a fundamental (roe, leverage, asset_turnover, operating_margin, earnings_per_share) at 21-63 day windows failed the cheap screen three times (|t| 0.07-0.53). TS_DELTA($leverage, 126) paired with a level term (CS_RANK($roe)) passed at fitness 3.859: prefer 126+ day windows for fundamental deltas, and pair a delta with a level rather than two deltas together.
  7. $accrual_gap (coverage 0.872) and the 126-day delta of $operating_margin (coverage 0.882) both missed the 0.90 bar by a similar margin, pointing to sparse reporting for these fields in this universe. Deprioritize them until coverage improves at the data layer.
  8. 5 of 20 rejections were archive_subtree near-duplicates, and each was only a window tweak (21 to 42, 2 to 5) or an added multiplier on an already-archived tree, never a structural change. The earnings_per_share/close ratio subtree alone accounted for 2 of them; change the operator or feature, not just the window, near these trees.
  9. A mechanically similar feature or operator swap without structural change reads as a duplicate, not a diversification: $volume in place of $dollar_volume scored rho 0.850 against an existing member, and EMA in place of TS_MEAN at the same window scored rho 0.996. Pair any such substitution with a genuine structural change.
  10. Both crossover_not_a_fusion rejections used CS_RANK($roa), a 2-node wrapped-leaf archive member, as a parent; that size can never meet the fusion donation requirement. Exclude bare single-feature CS_RANK(feature) members from the fusion parent pool.
  11. 3 of 20 rejections were exact within-run duplicates: CS_RANK($roa) plus two high-low-range/dollar-volume normalization variants. De-duplicate the candidate pool before scoring, especially around that feature family.
  12. The round's top 3 fitness scores (5.128, 4.780, 4.553) all paired a fundamental level or a close-vs-high price-distance term with a volume-liquidity normalizer (CS_ZSCORE or TS_RANK of $dollar_volume). This pairing is outperforming pure return/fundamental combos; prioritize it next round.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
Leave `parent_ids` empty and `changed_node` empty for EXPLORE.
